reference.title: Dumbbell Narrow Squat
reference.listing: Page could not be read (gymvisual.com blocked from this environment); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching

breathing.pattern: Breathe in and brace at the top, lower; breathe out as you pass the hardest part of the rise.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s down, short pause, about 1.2 s up

prescription.progression: Heavier dumbbells, a 2 s pause at the bottom. Dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight that leaves about 2-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-8) at the end of each set.

cues.text: Feet close together, toes forward or slightly out; a dumbbell in each hand at the sides, palms in, arms long.
Breathe in, brace, bend the knees forward over the toes and sit down between the heels; the dumbbells hang straight down.
Thighs about parallel, heels down, chest up.
Drive the floor away and stand tall; breathe out near the top.

mistakes.fix: Sit back a little more and stop at the depth where the heels stay down.
Keep the knees pointing the same way as the toes.
Arms long and relaxed, shoulders down; the dumbbells just hang.

mistakes.mistake: Rounding the back at the bottom
mistakes.fix: Stop above the depth where the pelvis tucks; keep the chest up.

kinematics.norm: Feet close together, narrower than hip width (common coaching)
About 100-110 degrees with the thighs near parallel (clinical opinion); a narrow stance needs more ankle dorsiflexion for the same depth (clinical opinion; Zawadka 2020 on depth and knee range)
Not specified by the sources for this depth
A little more lean than a hip-width squat (clinical opinion); more lean moves demand from knee to hip (Straub 2024)
Hanging straight down at the sides (common coaching)
About 2 s down, about 1 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #19810, Dumbbell Narrow Squat, video (movement reference)
Zawadka et al. 2020, How are squat timing and kinematics in the sagittal plane related to squat depth? (J Sports Sci Med 19:500-507)
Straub and Powers 2024, a biomechanical review of the squat exercise: implications for clinical practice (Int J Sports Phys Ther)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or giving-way occurs.
Choose a dumbbell load you can control for every rep; the load is user-chosen.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Heels lift or knees ache: squat to a shallower depth or a box.
Tight ankles: a small heel raise or a slightly wider stance.

muscleNotes.quads_r: Knee extensors lower and drive the squat; the narrow stance and forward knee travel keep the load on the quadriceps (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Knee extensors lower and drive the squat; the narrow stance and forward knee travel keep the load on the quadriceps (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Hip extensor, working hardest out of the bottom (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Hip extensor, working hardest out of the bottom (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Help extend the hip out of the bottom and keep the knees in line (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Help extend the hip out of the bottom and keep the knees in line (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Co-contract around the knee and assist hip extension out of the bottom (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Co-contract around the knee and assist hip extension out of the bottom (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.calves_r: Steady the shins as the knees travel forward over the toes.
muscleNotes.calves_l: Steady the shins as the knees travel forward over the toes.
muscleNotes.core: Braces against the load held in front of the body.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Keep the back flat as the trunk leans a little forward (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Keep the back flat as the trunk leans a little forward (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the knees tracking over the toes (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Keeps the knees tracking over the toes (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Grip the dumbbell handle for the whole set (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Grip the dumbbell handle for the whole set (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Hold the shoulders level against the hanging dumbbells (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Hold the shoulders level against the hanging dumbbells (clinical opinion).
